name: Aaron Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This interview is confidential, and you can separate what you would say publicly from your private thoughts. What does a normal working day involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Aaron, 43, a junior developer at a tech company that builds parcel-tracking dashboards. I took a two-year college diploma after working in a print shop, so I am still learning the code and I need senior review on anything beyond a simple display fix. I open the ticket queue, trace a missing parcel scan, and write the correction in a paper notebook before I touch the code. I have never used an AI tool; I want to know how a result was reached.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How much room does your family have if work changes?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Claire, works in a school library, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My junior developer pay is high for the job, and we have about nine months of expenses saved. There are plenty of similar jobs nearby, but a vacancy is not the same as an offer for someone still learning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my colleagues AI Plateau leaves the parcel dashboard needing people who can follow a missing scan. A routine tool can sort tickets, but it should not invent a delivery time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I would be relieved that my slow method still works. With nine months saved and two wages, I expect the mortgage to stay manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep tracing missing scans in my notebook and have a senior developer review each fix. I’d leave our 400 monthly savings transfer in place while both jobs hold. In the first year I’d ask the team to check routine ticket sorting against actual parcel records.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the household, though I still dislike a wrong delivery message. I do not expect my pay or hours to fall in this picture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which parcel error do you remember?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A customer was told a parcel had arrived when the final scan was missing. I found the missing parcel scan on paper before my senior colleague approved the fix.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your children make of the notebook?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children the notebook is not magic; it slows me enough to find a missing step. They know I still ask for help at work.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave parcel scans needing human checks.
I would reject **invented delivery times** from routine ticket sorting.
think: I feel **relieved** that my careful method still earns a wage.
Our **nine-month cushion** and two incomes make the mortgage manageable.
do: **Keep** tracing missing scans in a notebook with senior review.
**Transfer** 400 monthly into savings while both jobs hold.
**Check** automated ticket sorting against actual parcel records.
feel: **Calm** about income, with concern for wrong customer messages.
S0.quote: I found the missing parcel scan on paper before my senior colleague approved the fix.
fieldNote: His **paper notebook** helps a learner trace errors rather than trust a result he cannot explain.
High pay, **nine months saved** and many local jobs support a calm response to modest AI.

steps.text: Keep tracing missing scans in his notebook with senior review
Transfer 400 monthly into savings while both jobs hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will let software sort tickets, draft fixes and answer parcel questions. I would ask our worker committee for a written review of what happens to junior staff.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I worry I am exactly the person a faster ticket system replaces. Claire’s library work includes catalog records and simple answers, so her hours may also be squeezed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the senior developer to show me one approved AI ticket sorter using copied old cases. If it correctly finds a missing scan three times, I’d learn to review its results during paid hours. In the first year, if junior posts are cut, I’d take the evidence to the worker committee and ask for paid training time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about two incomes, even with nine months saved. Nine months of savings lets us argue for terms; it does not make my skill gap disappear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the worker committee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring three cases where a package was marked delivered without a final scan. I would ask who signs the customer reply if the software guesses wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Claire ask at the library?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Claire would ask whether library staff still correct the catalog and help children find books. I would not tell her that a new system automatically means her hours are gone.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to speed ticket sorting, code fixes and customer replies.
I would seek a **written staff review** through our worker committee.
think: I fear a **junior replacement** because ticket fixes are my main work.
I worry Claire’s **library hours** could shrink with automated records and replies.
do: **Test** an approved ticket sorter on copied old cases with senior help.
**Learn** to review its output during paid time if it finds missing scans three times.
**Bring** cut evidence to the worker committee if junior posts are reduced.
feel: **Anxious** about both wages and my skill gap despite a long buffer.
S1.quote: Nine months of savings lets us argue for terms; it does not make my skill gap disappear.
fieldNote: His **first AI trial** has a three-case proof gate and paid learning condition.
His **collective action** depends on junior cuts; he fears Claire’s library hours as well as his own.

steps.text: Learn approved ticket sorting during paid hours if three copied cases pass
Bring junior cut evidence to the worker committee if posts shrink

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 reaches parcel-code and library-record thinking work by 2028. Robots for hands-on work arrive around 2031, but both of our jobs have screen tasks now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my junior role to end and Claire’s library hours to fall. Nine months saved is real protection, but it cannot guarantee two new jobs or pay the mortgage forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company for written severance and the union for advice on negotiating it. I’d hold off on replacing the family car and keep the cash. In the first year after 2028, if I am laid off, I’d apply for real local openings and seek income help if we qualify.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, because two wages could fall close together. I can make a list of calls, yet the thought of explaining a long job search to the children keeps me awake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens to the car replacement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the old car if it remains safe to drive and cancel the replacement order. Safety repairs would still be paid because Claire needs the car for work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union do for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union for a written explanation of any severance offer. I would not sign a release on the same day a manager hands it to me.

say: I expect **AGI by 2028** to reach both parcel code and library records then.
I would remind colleagues **2031 robots** arrive after our screen-work change.
think: I expect my **junior role** to end and Claire’s hours to fall.
Our **nine-month reserve** cannot guarantee two replacement wages.
do: **Seek** union advice on written severance terms now.
**Cancel** the car replacement while paying for safety repairs.
**Apply** for actual local vacancies and eligible income help if dismissed after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely loss of two wages despite substantial savings.
S2.quote: Nine months saved is real protection, but it cannot guarantee two new jobs or pay the mortgage forever.
fieldNote: Both adults face **thinking-work change** in 2028, before robots arrive around 2031.
His **union advice** is individual severance guidance; income help depends on eligibility, and car safety repairs stay funded.

steps.text: Cancel the family car replacement while funding safety repairs
Apply for actual local openings if dismissed after 2028
Seek eligible income help if dismissed after 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives five years to sort out how we treat junior staff. Thinking AI reaches my code and Claire’s library records in 2031; hands-on robots arrive around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect fewer junior coding posts, but five years lets me learn a narrower technical skill while earning. I am still unsure whether that skill would be paid after full thinking AI arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for a paid company course in parcel-system testing and practise one old fault each week with the senior developer. If funding is refused, I’d use the free manual rather than pay tuition from the mortgage reserve. In the first year after 2031, if my role ends, I’d apply for real testing openings that still pay enough for our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, because I expect my work to shrink, but I have time to test what I can do. AGI by 2031 should not become an excuse for denying junior developers training now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which fault would you practise first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use a missing final scan as the first fault and ask the senior developer to mark my test. If I cannot find it without a hint, I need more practice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would happen to family spending?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Claire and I would keep the current car and review the school costs each term. We would not use our reserve for a certificate with no real vacancy attached.

say: I see **AGI by 2031** as time to set fair terms for junior staff.
I know **2034 robots** come after the code and library change.
think: I expect **fewer junior posts** despite a longer warning.
I cannot assume a **testing job** survives full thinking AI.
do: **Request** a paid parcel-testing course and practise one old fault weekly.
**Use** the free manual if company funding is refused.
**Apply** for real mortgage-paying testing posts if dismissed after 2031.
feel: **Anxious** about shrinking work, with time to practise and save.
S3.quote: AGI by 2031 should not become an excuse for denying junior developers training now.
fieldNote: His **course request** depends on employer funding, with a free manual fallback.
The **five-year window** makes practice possible, but he treats later testing vacancies as uncertain.

steps.text: Practise parcel testing weekly and take company-paid course or free manual
Apply for real testing posts that cover the mortgage if dismissed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2036 gives a decade to negotiate how junior workers are treated. Thinking AI reaches parcel code and library records in 2036; robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect our income to hold for the next few years, but I do not want management using a distant forecast to delay wage talks. Our nine months saved let us ask hard questions without rushing into a new job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep working through parcel tickets with senior review and keep the 400 monthly savings transfer while both wages hold. I’d attend the worker committee’s quarterly staffing review. In the first year after 2036, if the coding role ends, I’d check current vacancies before applying elsewhere and keep the mortgage reserve for bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the long term, but I feel secure enough to keep learning now. AGI by 2036 gives management time to train junior developers, not permission to ignore us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask at a staffing review?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the number of junior posts and training hours at each quarterly review. If those numbers fall, the committee should raise it before a surprise layoff.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the family change summer plans?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Claire we can keep the children’s summer camp if our pay holds. I would not use mortgage savings to pay for an unapproved course.

say: I see **AGI by 2036** as time to negotiate fair terms for junior workers.
I know **2039 robots** follow the earlier code and library shift.
think: I expect **both wages** to hold for the next few years.
I worry a distant forecast may delay **wage talks** now.
do: **Keep** fixing parcel tickets with senior review and save 400 monthly while wages hold.
**Attend** quarterly worker committee staffing reviews and request junior training figures.
**Check** real vacancies after 2036 if my coding role ends.
feel: **Uneasy** about long-term work, with current income secure.
S4.quote: AGI by 2036 gives management time to train junior developers, not permission to ignore us.
fieldNote: His **strong reserve** makes collective wage and staffing questions possible without a rushed job change.
He keeps **summer camp** conditional on current pay and protects mortgage cash from unfunded courses.

steps.text: Keep fixing parcel tickets under senior review
Save 400 monthly while both wages hold
Attend quarterly worker committee staffing reviews
Check real job vacancies if coding work ends after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my code and Claire’s library records could change together. Written severance, union advice and income help we qualify for would help. Nine months buys a search; it does not buy a second career.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who corrects a parcel record when a child’s medicine is marked delivered but never reaches the house. A parcel dashboard cannot put a missing medicine package at the door.

headlineQuote: A parcel dashboard cannot put a missing medicine package at the door.
portrait: Aaron is a **43-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma, high pay and nine months of expenses saved.
He has **never used AI** and traces parcel faults in a notebook before asking a senior developer to review code.
His partner’s **library records** face thinking AI alongside his coding tasks, putting both wages at risk under fast AGI.
He seeks **union advice**, funded or free testing practice and real vacancies while protecting mortgage cash.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut his junior role and his partner’s library hours together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, union advice and eligible income help would support the family.
